models.name: Mesh-Resolved Two-Phase CFD (MR-TP)
models.what_it_computes: Transient, pore-scale primary atomization and near-field droplet size spectrum using interface-capturing with surface tension and contact-line physics

models.name: Aerosol Transport and Breakup CFD (ATB)
models.what_it_computes: Far-field aerosol evolution through the plenum and mouthpiece, including secondary breakup, coalescence, evaporation, and transport; outputs droplet size distribution at the mouthpiece exit

mechanisms.name: Primary atomization at the vibrating mesh
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sets the initial droplet size spectrum emitted from individual orifices, a dominant determinant of delivered dose and regional lung deposition

mechanisms.name: Downstream secondary processes
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Aerodynamic shear, coalescence, and evaporation in the mouthpiece and near-field plume reshape the size distribution prior to inhalation

deviation.detail: Each credibility factor is rated on an Assurance Index from 0 to 12, where higher values indicate stronger evidence

findings.mechanism: Primary atomization at the vibrating mesh
spans: When the pore-scale cell size and interface-resolving layers were halved near the orifice exits, the Sauter mean diameter shifted by 1.2% and the median by 0.9%, indicating that further refinement at the orifice scale yields only marginal changes in the near-field spectrum.
The near-field spectrum showed near-monotone convergence in D32 and the percentile metrics.
The asymptotic trend was assessed over three grids with approximately 3.8 million, 7.5 million, and 15.2 million cells in the two-phase domain, plus dynamic refinement layers.
findings.span: When the pore-scale cell size and interface-resolving layers were halved near the orifice exits, the Sauter mean diameter shifted by 1.2% and the median by 0.9%, indicating that further refinement at the orifice scale yields only marginal changes in the near-field spectrum.

findings.mechanism: Primary atomization at the vibrating mesh
spans: We tightened nonlinear residual targets to 107 and linear solvers to 109 relative tolerances.
The near-field spectral stability across successive cycles was monitored to ensure stationarity before data collection.
findings.span: We tightened nonlinear residual targets to 107 and linear solvers to 109 relative tolerances.

findings.mechanism: Primary atomization at the vibrating mesh
spans: Alternative interface-capturing choices had a small but measurable influence: switching from a continuum surface force curvature calculation to a geometrical reconstruction altered the D32 by 2.7%, and replacing a dynamic contact-angle model with a static angle changed the tail fraction above 5 µm by 1.1%.

The curvature and wetting choices produce the largest structural influence on the near-field spectrum among the toggles, whereas advection-scheme effects were negligible compared with measurement repeatability.
findings.span: Alternative interface-capturing choices had a small but measurable influence: switching from a continuum surface force curvature calculation to a geometrical reconstruction altered the D32 by 2.7%, and replacing a dynamic contact-angle model with a static angle changed the tail fraction above 5 µm by 1.1%.

findings.mechanism: Primary atomization at the vibrating mesh
spans: For the baseline drive settings, the predicted mean diameter at that plane is 3.0 µm against a measured 3.1 µm (n = 6 repeats), with a bin-wise mean absolute error of 0.32 µm across 0.2 µm bins and percentile differences of 0.09 µm (Dv10), 0.10 µm (Dv50), and 0.14 µm (Dv90).
Near-field spectra were compared against PDPA measurements at 2 mm above the mesh.
findings.span: For the baseline drive settings, the predicted mean diameter at that plane is 3.0 µm against a measured 3.1 µm (n = 6 repeats), with a bin-wise mean absolute error of 0.32 µm across 0.2 µm bins and percentile differences of 0.09 µm (Dv10), 0.10 µm (Dv50), and 0.14 µm (Dv90).

findings.mechanism: Downstream secondary processes
spans: Doubling the cell size beyond 1 mm above the mesh to economize on the far-field region shifted Dv50 by 6.4%, reflecting that resolution away from the orifice is insufficient to compensate for missing transport physics over centimeter scales.
Coarsening the far-field region revealed appreciable changes in distribution metrics, symptomatic of a model not designed for these scales.
findings.span: Doubling the cell size beyond 1 mm above the mesh to economize on the far-field region shifted Dv50 by 6.4%, reflecting that resolution away from the orifice is insufficient to compensate for missing transport physics over centimeter scales.

findings.mechanism: Downstream secondary processes
spans: Structural omissions dominate: because breakup and coalescence are not modeled beyond near-field ligament pinch-off, the predicted distribution underestimates the large-droplet tail; specifically, the volume fraction above 5 µm is underpredicted by 12% relative to measurements taken 20 mm from the mesh.
findings.span: Structural omissions dominate: because breakup and coalescence are not modeled beyond near-field ligament pinch-off, the predicted distribution underestimates the large-droplet tail; specifically, the volume fraction above 5 µm is underpredicted by 12% relative to measurements taken 20 mm from the mesh.

findings.mechanism: Downstream secondary processes
spans: We tested inlet turbulence intensity values between 2% and 6% to emulate uncertainty in the plenum inflow under inhalation; the result is an 8.1% spread in Dv90 at 20 mm.
We bracketed plausible values based on separate ATB simula-tions and device characterizations, then observed their influence on the far-field distribution.
findings.span: We tested inlet turbulence intensity values between 2% and 6% to emulate uncertainty in the plenum inflow under inhalation; the result is an 8.1% spread in Dv90 at 20 mm.

findings.mechanism: Downstream secondary processes
spans: Time-step adjustments from 0.2 µs to 0.4 µs—in the absence of a fully resolved gas-side turbulence model—induce a 3.8% change in D32, indicating that numerical settings begin to leak into physical variability in this misapplied region of MR-TP.
Temporal integration and solver tolerances tuned for near-field capillary dynamics are less directly relevant to the diluted downstream use of MR-TP.
findings.span: Time-step adjustments from 0.2 µs to 0.4 µs—in the absence of a fully resolved gas-side turbulence model—induce a 3.8% change in D32, indicating that numerical settings begin to leak into physical variability in this misapplied region of MR-TP.

spans: A recorded temperature rise of 1.4 °C over the experimental run, not imposed in the simulation, likely increases evaporation marginally and further differentiates the measured spectrum from the prediction.

findings.mechanism: Primary atomization at the vibrating mesh
spans: Halving the injection bin width from 0.2 µm to 0.1 µm changed Dv50 at 2 mm by 7.1%, a magnitude far larger than would be acceptable for a near-field resolution study.

findings.mechanism: Primary atomization at the vibrating mesh
spans: Substituting a Rosin–Rammler injection kernel for a tabulated spectrum from MR-TP shifted Dv10 by 10.8%, demonstrating the leverage of parametric choices on early-field metrics.

findings.mechanism: Primary atomization at the vibrating mesh
spans: Input perturbations that remain within the PDPA’s confidence bounds for the near-field spectrum propagate through ATB to a 5.2% change in D32 at 2 mm.

findings.mechanism: Primary atomization at the vibrating mesh
spans: Time-integration and solver settings in ATB are not the limiting factor in this regime: halving the maximum adaptive time step from 5×105 s to 2.5×105 s changed Dv50 by 1.5%, and the iterative solver with a 106 residual target showed no discernible trend in percentile metrics.

findings.mechanism: Downstream secondary processes
spans: Increasing the plenum-to-mouthpiece mesh from 3.1 million to 11.6 million cells while maintaining y+ below 1 at the walls altered the mouthpiece Dv50 by 1.3%.

findings.mechanism: Downstream secondary processes
